purpose: Qualify a separate one-dimensional transient-conduction coupon through the V11H/V11I equivalent slab depth with constant properties, synthetic boundary conditions, analytical references, a conservative flux-enthalpy ledger and space-time refinement. No temperature history is coupled back to the mechanical panel in this iteration.

scope.domain: One square metre, one-dimensional coordinate x from the idealized slab bottom face x=0 to the top face x=L. Constant k, rho and cp; no in-plane conduction, deck, reinforcement, moisture, phase change, radiation, convection, SFRM or contact resistance.
scope.boundary_conditions: Adiabatic, prescribed-temperature and prescribed-inward-flux faces used only as synthetic verification inputs. Positive face flux means heat entering the coupon.
scope.coupling_policy: The calculated profiles remain outside V11I. They are not panel loads, gas temperatures, fire exposures or WTC histories. Mechanical work, thermal strain, damage and fracture are not evaluated.
scope.history_policy: No V11E/V11F/V11I damage variable, stress state, material property or energy ledger is edited. Constant-property conduction stores sensible enthalpy only.
scope.energy_policy: For unit area, Delta H equals the time integral of bottom-inward plus top-inward heat flux. H is in J/m2, flux in W/m2 and temperature in degC with increments identical to K. Global collapse-energy credit is exactly zero.

geometry.coordinate: x=0 bottom face; x=L top face; cell-centred finite volumes
geometry.status: The 4.35 in equivalent thickness is inherited from the bounded slab-section model and is not a complete as-built metal-deck/concrete geometry.

constant_properties.density_and_cp_status: The rho and cp values are inherited unchanged from V11H generic constant hypotheses solely to isolate and verify conduction. They are not measured WTC slab properties.
constant_properties.conductivity_status: The 1.0 W/(m K) reference is a verification anchor. The 0.5 to 1.3 W/(m K) bracket spans simple constant values identified by NIST for lightweight and normal-weight concrete estimates and the WTC fire-model boundary assumption. It is not a calibrated property of the actual floor slab.

numerical_method.scheme: Backward Euler in time, conservative cell-centred finite volume in space, harmonic-interface form reducing to k/dx for constant k, direct tridiagonal Thomas solve.
numerical_method.dirichlet_face_conductance: 2*k/dx between a face value and the adjacent cell centre
numerical_method.absolute_temperature_note: Only temperature differences enter this constant-property equation; degC increments and K increments are numerically identical.

discretization.space_refinement_mode: Exact-in-time eigenvalue of the cell-centred finite-volume spatial operator for the smooth sine mode; this isolates spatial truncation from backward-Euler error.

cases.analytical_reference: T(x,t)=60 degC and both inward fluxes are zero.
The exact linear profile is stationary; q_bottom_in=-k*100/L, q_top_in=+k*100/L and net inward heat is zero.
No closed field comparator is used; mean(T)-20=q*t/(rho*cp*L) and DeltaH=q*t exactly.

method_sources.locator: Chapter 6 p.98 and Appendix A p.274 of the report pagination
method_sources.scope: Primary official model report: 4.35 in equivalent slab thickness; approximately 16 through-depth thermal elements were used to resolve thermal waves and steep surface gradients; lightweight-concrete conductivity was temperature dependent in the official thermal model. V11J does not reproduce that model.

Primary official fire-model report: the exposed slab underside used k=1.0 W/(m K), rho=2000 kg/m3 and cp=0.88 kJ/(kg K) as gas-phase boundary properties, while detailed member penetration was calculated separately. Only k=1.0 is used here as a numerical anchor, not as an as-built calibration.

Primary NIST design guidance: simple averaged constant conductivity estimates of 1.3 W/(m K) for normal-weight and 0.5 W/(m K) for lightweight normal-strength concrete, with cautions about density, aggregate, moisture and small-scale data. Used only to bracket conductivity sensitivity.
